s1.syndrome_frame: A chronic cutaneous lesion with crusty plaques and papules in the fronto-orbital region
salient_findings: Irregularly shaped 5 × 3 cm plaque with multiple superficial crusts
Eosinophilic keratinocytes with pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli infiltrating the reticular dermis
Marked regression of the plaque after treatment, but with remaining discrete papular lesions
key_facts: 59-year-old man
Crusty lesion in the right fronto-orbital region
No significant past medical history
Lesion present for several months
Excisional biopsy showed lobules and detached aggregates of eosinophilic keratinocytes
Pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli
Infiltration of the reticular dermis
Treatment with cemiplimab 350 mg every 3 weeks
Initial PET/CT showed focal area of uptake in the supraorbital lesion
Marked regression of the plaque after five cycles of treatment
Remaining discrete papular lesions with features typical of basal cell carcinoma

shortlist.label: Invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Diagnosed by excisional biopsy and consistent with the clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Dermoscopic evaluation of remaining papules revealed features typical of basal cell carcinoma

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma in situ
shortlist.why_kept: Possible precursor to invasive squamous cell carcinoma and consistent with the clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Bowen's disease
shortlist.why_kept: A form of squamous cell carcinoma in situ and a possible consideration given the patient's presentation

shortlist.label: Keratoacanthoma
shortlist.why_kept: A low-grade malignancy that can resemble squamous cell carcinoma and may be considered in the differential diagnosis
